questions.q: The rectum measures approximately how much in length?
questions.exp: The chapter states that the rectum is 12-14 cm in length. (Book p233)

questions.q: The upper and the lower parts of the rectum are convex towards the:
questions.exp: Upper and lower parts of the rectum are convex towards the right. (Book p233)

questions.q: The middle part of the rectum is convex towards the:
questions.exp: The middle part of the rectum is convex towards the left — the rectum has three lateral curves. (Book p233)

questions.q: Which part of the rectum is not covered with peritoneum?
questions.exp: Only the lower part of the rectum is not covered with peritoneum; the upper part is intraperitoneal. (Book p233)

questions.q: Resection of the rectum below the peritoneum is the applied anatomy of:
questions.exp: The applied anatomy note says that resection of rectum below the peritoneum is a low anterior resection. (Book p233)

questions.q: The anorectal ring is formed by the:
questions.exp: The anorectal ring is formed by the levator ani. (Book p233)

questions.q: The distance from the anorectal ring to the dentate line is approximately:
questions.exp: The diagram labels the anorectal ring to dentate line distance as 2-2.5 cm. (Book p233)

questions.q: The distance from the dentate line to the anal verge is approximately:
questions.exp: The dentate line to anal verge distance is also labelled 2-2.5 cm, so the whole surgical anal canal is roughly 4-5 cm. (Book p233)

questions.q: Sensation above the dentate line is characterised by:
questions.exp: Above the dentate line there are no pain sensations — that is why painless banding and injection are done there. (Book p233)

questions.q: Pain sensation below the dentate line is:
opts: Present only on the right side
questions.exp: Below the dentate line pain sensations are present — the lining is somatic sensitive squamous epithelium. (Book p233)

questions.q: Injury to the anal sphincters results in:
questions.exp: The page notes that injury to the sphincters causes incontinence. (Book p233)

questions.q: The epithelium proximal to the dentate line is:
questions.exp: Proximal to the dentate line the epithelium is columnar. (Book p233)

questions.q: The tumour that arises from the epithelium proximal to the dentate line is:
questions.exp: Columnar epithelium above the dentate line gives rise to adenocarcinoma. (Book p233)

questions.q: The epithelium distal to the dentate line is:
questions.exp: Distal to the dentate line the epithelium is modified squamous. (Book p233)

questions.q: A malignant growth of the epithelium distal to the dentate line is a:
questions.exp: Modified squamous epithelium below the dentate line gives rise to squamous cell carcinoma. (Book p233)

questions.q: A 60-year-old has a painful 1 cm ulcer at the anal margin. Pain localises the lesion to:
questions.exp: Pain means somatic sensory epithelium, i.e. the lesion lies below the dentate line; lesions above it are painless. (Book p233)

questions.q: The columns of Morgagni are:
opts: Folds of mucosa above the dentate line
Folds of mucosa below the dentate line
questions.exp: Columns of Morgagni are folds of the mucosa above the dentate line. (Book p233)

questions.q: The communication between the anal crypts and the anal glands is clinically important because it is the:
opts: Route of lymphatic spread to the liver
questions.exp: The cryptoglandular communication is the site of abscess — the basis of the cryptoglandular hypothesis of fistula-in-ano. (Book p233)

questions.q: The submucosa of the distal anal canal contains:
questions.exp: There are 3 haemorrhoidal cushions (vascular channels) in the submucosa of the distal anal canal. (Book p233)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classical positions of the anal cushions?
questions.exp: The three primary positions are left anterior, right anterior and right posterior — not left posterior. (Book p233)

questions.q: Prolapse of the anal cushions produces:
questions.exp: The cushions prolapse to produce haemorrhoids; their position is the classical position of primary haemorrhoids. (Book p233)

questions.sec: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters
questions.q: The internal anal sphincter receives parasympathetic fibres from:
questions.exp: Internal sphincter: parasympathetic from S2, S3, S4. (Book p233)

questions.sec: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters
questions.q: The sympathetic supply of the internal anal sphincter comes from:
questions.exp: Internal sphincter also receives sympathetic fibres from L5. (Book p233)

questions.sec: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters
questions.q: The external anal sphincter is supplied by the:
questions.exp: External sphincter: pudendal nerve, S2, S3, S4. (Book p233)

questions.sec: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters
questions.q: Bilateral injury of the pudendal nerve causes:
questions.exp: Bilateral (B/L) injury of the pudendal nerve causes incontinence. (Book p233)

questions.sec: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters
questions.q: Unilateral injury of the pudendal nerve causes:
questions.exp: Unilateral (U/L) injury does not cause incontinence because the opposite side maintains the sphincter. (Book p233)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: Digital rectal examination is performed with the patient in the:
questions.exp: The position for DRE is Sim's (left lateral) position. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: Before performing a DRE the examinee must remember to do what the page lists first?
opts: Inform the procedure and receive consent
questions.exp: The page lists informing the procedure and receiving consent as the first step. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: All of the following are looked for on inspection of the anal region EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Inspection looks for external opening of fistula, external haemorrhoids, a painful fissure and growth — the prostate is assessed by the examining finger, not by inspection. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: DRE is contraindicated when inspection shows:
questions.exp: A fissure is painful, so DRE is contraindicated. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: The digit used for DRE in adults is the:
questions.exp: In adults the (R) index finger is used. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: The digit used for DRE in children is the:
questions.exp: In children the little finger is used. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: On DRE the anterior (12 o'clock) relation in a male is the:
questions.exp: Anteriorly in males the finger feels the prostate. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: On DRE the anterior relation in a female is the:
questions.exp: Anteriorly in females the finger feels the cervix and the pouch of Douglas. (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: The lateral wall of the rectum on the clock face corresponds to:
questions.exp: The lateral wall is described as 3 o'clock (with the opposite lateral wall completing the clock face). (Book p234)

questions.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
questions.q: The posterior relation felt on DRE corresponds to:
questions.exp: The posterior position (sacral hollow) is 6 o'clock. (Book p234)

questions.q: The approximate length of an anoscope is:
questions.exp: Anoscope: ~10 cm. (Book p234)

questions.q: The approximate length of a proctoscope is:
questions.exp: Proctoscope: ~13 cm. (Book p234)

questions.q: The length of a colonoscope as quoted in this chapter is:
questions.exp: Colonoscope: length 110-140 cm. (Book p234)

questions.q: The instrument that is visualised from the anal canal till the caecum is the:
questions.exp: The colonoscope is described as visualising from the anal canal till the caecum. (Book p234)

questions.q: The 60 cm instrument listed under visualization is taken up to the:
questions.exp: The 60 cm instrument (sigmoidoscope) is visualised until the sigmoid colon. (Book p234)

questions.q: Arrange the instruments in increasing order of the length of bowel they can inspect:
questions.exp: Anoscope ~10 cm, proctoscope ~13 cm, sigmoidoscope ~60 cm (till sigmoid colon), colonoscope 110-140 cm (till caecum). (Book p234)

questions.q: Haemorrhoids are:
questions.exp: Haemorrhoids are dilated vascular channels. (Book p235)

questions.q: The bleeding in haemorrhoids is:
questions.exp: The chapter emphasises that haemorrhoidal bleeding is arterial. (Book p235)

questions.q: The most common cause of bleeding per rectum is:
questions.exp: Haemorrhoids are stated to be the most common (m/c) cause of bleeding per rectum. (Book p235)

questions.q: Bleeding per rectum in haemorrhoids is usually:
questions.exp: Bleeding P/R is painless (usually). (Book p235)

questions.q: Painful bleeding per rectum is seen with all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Painful bleeding is seen with external haemorrhoids (because of their location below the dentate line) and with thrombosed haemorrhoids; uncomplicated internal haemorrhoids above the dentate line bleed painlessly. (Book p235)

questions.q: External haemorrhoids are painful because they lie:
questions.exp: External haemorrhoids lie below the dentate line, where pain sensation is present. (Book p235)

questions.q: Which associated symptom is listed under the clinical features of haemorrhoids?
questions.exp: Constipation is listed as a clinical feature/association of haemorrhoids. (Book p235)

questions.q: The investigation of choice for haemorrhoids is:
questions.exp: Investigation of choice: proctoscopy (haemorrhoids are visualised by the proctoscope). (Book p235)

questions.q: A thrombosed pile is described in this chapter as:
opts: A life-long lesion needing immediate surgery
questions.exp: Thrombosed piles are described as a 5 day self healing lesion. (Book p235)

questions.q: Which statement about palpation in anorectal disease is correct?
opts: Thrombosed piles are palpable on DRE but haemorrhoids are not
Both haemorrhoids and thrombosed piles are always palpable
questions.exp: DRE: thrombosed piles are palpable, whereas haemorrhoids are not palpable. (Book p235)

questions.q: A thrombosed pile presents as:
opts: A painless swelling that is never felt
questions.exp: The chapter lists a mass felt on DRE in thrombosed piles. (Book p235)

questions.q: Emergency surgery for a thrombosed pile offers:
opts: Excision or evacuation of the clot
questions.exp: Emergency surgery is either excision or evacuation of the clot. (Book p235)

questions.q: Conservative treatment of a thrombosed pile is followed by definitive surgery after:
questions.exp: Conservative management lets the lesion heal (about 5 days) and definitive surgery is done after a few days to weeks. (Book p235)

questions.q: Which intervention is the investigation of choice in thrombosed piles?
questions.exp: Investigation of choice: proctoscopy. (Book p235)

questions.q: Grade I haemorrhoids:
opts: Only bleed and do not prolapse
questions.exp: Grade I: only bleed, do not prolapse. (Book p235)

questions.q: Grade II haemorrhoids:
questions.exp: Grade II: prolapse, spontaneously reduced. (Book p235)

questions.q: Grade III haemorrhoids:
questions.exp: Grade III: prolapse, manually reduced. (Book p235)

questions.q: Grade IV haemorrhoids:
questions.exp: Grade IV: remain prolapsed. (Book p235)

questions.q: A patient who has to push a bleeding prolapsing mass back with his finger after every motion has:
questions.exp: Prolapse needing manual reduction is grade III. (Book p235)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Conservative management of grade I haemorrhoids includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Grade I is managed conservatively — laxatives, sitz bath and life style changes; surgery belongs to the higher grades. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: A sitz bath helps because:
questions.exp: Sitz bath: lukewarm water relaxes the sphincter. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Management of grade II haemorrhoids is:
opts: Management of grade I plus an office procedure
questions.exp: Grade II is managed as grade I plus an office procedure (banding / sclerotherapy). (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Rubber band ligation works by:
opts: Cutting off the blood supply so the haemorrhoid sloughs off
Injecting a sclerosant into the pile
Stapling the mucosa back into position
Ligating the hemorrhoidal artery under Doppler guidance
questions.exp: Banding cuts off the blood supply and the haemorrhoid sloughs off spontaneously. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Rubber band ligation must be applied:
questions.exp: Banding is done above the dentate line, which is painless. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Sclerotherapy injects the sclerosant:
questions.exp: Application of sclerosing agents is above the dentate line. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: The effect of sclerotherapy on the pile is to:
opts: Pull the haemorrhoids up so that they slough off
Create a fibrous ring at the anorectal ring
questions.exp: Sclerotherapy pulls the haemorrhoids up and they slough off. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: The most commonly used sclerosing agent for haemorrhoids is:
questions.exp: Sodium tetradecyl sulfate is listed as the most common (m/c) sclerosing agent. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a sclerosing agent for piles?
questions.exp: The listed agents are sodium tetradecyl sulfate, sodium morrhuate, polidocanol and phenol in almond oil. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Deep sclerotherapy can cause all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Deep sclerotherapy causes pain, infection and prostatitis when done anteriorly; retrograde ejaculation is listed as a complication of rectal prolapse surgery. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
questions.q: Prostatitis after sclerotherapy is due to injection:
opts: Into the rectum above the peritoneal reflection
questions.exp: Anterior injection of sclerosant can produce prostatitis. (Book p236)

questions.q: Grade III haemorrhoids are treated by:
questions.exp: Grade III: management of grade II ± surgery. (Book p236)

questions.q: Grade IV haemorrhoids are treated by:
questions.exp: Grade IV: surgery. (Book p236)

questions.q: The Milligan-Morgan operation is the:
questions.exp: Open haemorrhoidectomy is the Milligan-Morgan operation. (Book p236)

questions.q: The Ferguson operation is the:
questions.exp: Closed haemorrhoidectomy is the Ferguson operation. (Book p236)

questions.q: The surgery of choice for haemorrhoids according to this chapter is:
questions.exp: Stapled haemorrhoidopexy is stated to be the surgery of choice. (Book p236)

questions.q: DGHAL expands to:
questions.exp: DGHAL = Doppler guided haemorrhoidal artery ligation. (Book p236)

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-excisional, Doppler guided day-care option for piles?
questions.exp: Doppler guided haemorrhoidal artery ligation (DGHAL) is listed among the surgical options and does not excise tissue. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery
questions.q: Reactionary haemorrhage after piles surgery is bleeding that occurs:
questions.exp: Reactionary haemorrhage is listed as a complication (bleeding in the immediate post-operative period, within 24 hours). (Book p237)

questions.sec: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery
questions.q: Incontinence after piles surgery is due to:
questions.exp: Incontinence is caused by injury to the sphincter. (Book p237)

questions.sec: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery
questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a complication of the surgery for piles?
questions.exp: Complications listed under surgery are reactionary haemorrhage, incontinence (sphincter injury) and recurrence. (Book p237)

questions.sec: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery
questions.q: Which of the following is a complication of haemorrhoids themselves and not of their surgery?
questions.exp: Complications of haemorrhoids are thrombosis, gangrene, fibrosis, portal pyaemia and ulceration. (Book p237)

questions.sec: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery
questions.q: All of the following are complications of haemorrhoids EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Thrombosis, gangrene, fibrosis, portal pyaemia and ulceration are complications of haemorrhoids. (Book p237)

questions.q: An anal fissure is:
opts: A breach in the continuity of the anal epithelium
A communication between two epithelial surfaces
questions.exp: Anal fissure is a breach in the continuity of the anal epithelium. (Book p237)

questions.q: An anal fissure lies:
questions.exp: The fissure lies below the dentate line. (Book p237)

questions.q: The most common site of an anal fissure is:
questions.exp: The m/c position is 6 o'clock, i.e. the posterior midline. (Book p237)

questions.q: An anal fissure at 12 o'clock in a woman is classically associated with:
questions.exp: A 12 o'clock (anterior) fissure is seen in obstructed labour. (Book p237)

questions.q: Which two symptoms are listed as the clinical features of an anal fissure?
questions.exp: Clinical features: bleeding P/R and constipation. (Book p237)

questions.q: The classical triad seen in chronic anal fissure comprises the fissure, a hypertrophic papilla and:
questions.exp: The diagram shows the triad of skin tag, fissure and hypertrophic papilla. (Book p237)

questions.q: The investigation of choice for an anal fissure is:
questions.exp: External inspection is the investigation of choice (IOC); DRE is contraindicated. (Book p237)

questions.q: The sentinel pile is another name for the:
opts: Skin tag of a chronic fissure
questions.exp: Skin tag is AKA sentinel pile and is seen in chronic fissure. (Book p237)

questions.q: The skin tag of a fissure is formed by:
questions.exp: The sentinel pile results from accumulation of lymphatics. (Book p237)

questions.q: A 30-year-old man has severe cutting pain during defecation and a drop of blood on the stool. On examination the doctor avoids doing a DRE because:
opts: It is contraindicated in a painful fissure
It can convert the fissure into a fistula
questions.exp: DRE is contraindicated in fissure — diagnosis is by gentle external inspection. (Book p237)

questions.q: Dietary advice in anal fissure includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Life style changes recommended are a high fibre diet, increased liquid intake and avoiding fried/fatty food. (Book p237)

questions.q: The local anaesthetic jelly used before and after defecation in anal fissure is:
questions.exp: 2% xylocaine jelly is applied before and after defecation. (Book p237)

questions.q: Diltiazem cream is used in anal fissure because it:
questions.exp: Diltiazem cream is listed as relaxing the sphincter — it is a calcium channel blocker used as a chemical sphincterotomy. (Book p237)

questions.q: Topical nitrate gel for anal fissure is associated with which side effect?
questions.exp: The side effects listed for nitrate gel are headache and hypertension. (Book p237)

questions.q: Which of the following is a sphincter-relaxing measure used in fissure-in-ano?
opts: Both diltiazem cream and nitrate gel
questions.exp: Diltiazem cream (relaxes the sphincter) and nitrate gel are the pharmacological sphincter relaxants; xylocaine gives analgesia. (Book p237)

questions.q: The standard operation for chronic anal fissure is:
questions.exp: Lateral anal sphincterotomy is the first surgical option listed. (Book p238)

questions.q: In lateral anal sphincterotomy the structure divided is the:
questions.exp: The internal sphincter is cut. (Book p238)

questions.q: Division of the internal sphincter heals a fissure because:
opts: The sphincter relaxes and the fissure heals
questions.exp: Cutting the internal sphincter relaxes the sphincter and the fissure heals. (Book p238)

questions.q: The second surgical option listed for anal fissure is:
questions.exp: The second option is an anal advancement flap. (Book p238)

questions.q: Pilonidal sinus is also called:
questions.exp: Pilonidal sinus is called jeep driver's disease. (Book p238)

questions.q: The most common site of a pilonidal sinus is the:
questions.exp: The natal cleft is the m/c site. (Book p238)

questions.q: Pilonidal sinus in the interdigital area is classically seen in:
questions.exp: The interdigital area is affected in barbers (hair in the web space). (Book p238)

questions.q: Which site of pilonidal sinus is mentioned in addition to the natal cleft and the interdigital area?
questions.exp: The sites listed are natal cleft (m/c), interdigital area (barbers) and the face. (Book p238)

questions.q: Pilonidal sinus characteristically occurs in:
questions.exp: It is a disease of hairy men. (Book p238)

questions.q: The pathogenesis of pilonidal sinus is:
opts: Friction → inward growth of hair → abscess → sinus
Infection of an apocrine gland → abscess → sinus
Ischaemic necrosis of the natal cleft skin
questions.exp: Friction causes inward growth of hair, which produces an abscess and then a sinus. (Book p238)

questions.q: The clinical features of pilonidal sinus listed are:
questions.exp: Clinical features: swelling and discharge. (Book p238)

questions.q: Incision and drainage of a pilonidal abscess must be accompanied by:
opts: Removal of the hair to prevent recurrence
questions.exp: Drain the abscess and remove the hair — done to prevent recurrence. (Book p238)

questions.q: Conservative measures listed for pilonidal sinus are:
questions.exp: Antibiotics and analgesics are the conservative measures listed. (Book p238)

questions.q: Which flap repair is listed for pilonidal sinus?
questions.exp: The Rhomboid/Limberg flap is the first surgical option listed. (Book p238)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a surgical option for pilonidal sinus?
questions.exp: The surgical options listed are the Rhomboid/Limberg flap, Bascom's technique and the Karydakis technique; Delorme's repair is a procedure for rectal prolapse. (Book p238)

questions.q: Bascom's technique for pilonidal sinus uses:
opts: An incision lateral to the midline with the sinus cleared and sutured
A mesh placed over the natal cleft
questions.exp: Bascom's technique is illustrated as an incision lateral to the midline, the sinus cleared and then sutured. (Book p238)

questions.q: All of the following are clinical features of an anorectal abscess EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Fever and swelling are listed, and fluctuation is specifically described as a LATE sign. (Book p239)

questions.q: Fluctuation is a late sign in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The page lists fluctuation as a late sign in parotid abscess, breast abscess and palmar/plantar abscess. (Book p239)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the anorectal abscess types illustrated on this page?
questions.exp: The four types illustrated are perianal, intersphincteric, ischiorectal and supralevator — not suprasphincteric (which is a fistula type). (Book p239)

questions.q: The most superficial of the anorectal abscesses is the:
questions.exp: The perianal abscess is the most superficial, lying just under the perianal skin. (Book p239)

questions.q: The abscess that lies above the levator ani in the diagram is the:
questions.exp: The supralevator abscess is drawn above the levator ani. (Book p239)

questions.q: The intersphincteric abscess lies between the:
opts: Levator ani and the pelvic peritoneum
Anal skin and the external sphincter
questions.exp: As the name implies, the intersphincteric abscess lies in the plane between the internal and external anal sphincters. (Book p239)

questions.q: The treatment of an anorectal abscess is:
questions.exp: Management is incision and drainage. (Book p239)

questions.q: A poorly drained anorectal abscess is likely to result in:
questions.exp: The page states that a poorly drained abscess becomes a perianal sinus/fistula. (Book p239)

questions.q: A perianal sinus/fistula is most often:
opts: Due to tuberculosis in most cases
questions.exp: Perianal sinus/fistula is secondary to anal sepsis. (Book p239)

questions.q: The term 'water-can perineum' refers to:
opts: Multiple external openings of a fistula
questions.exp: Water-can perineum is used when there are multiple external openings. (Book p239)

questions.q: The openings of a fistula-in-ano are described as:
opts: One internal and one or more external openings
questions.exp: A fistula has an internal opening (in the anal canal) and one or more external openings. (Book p239)

questions.q: The mnemonic 'Krohn, krush, Kancer, Koch's' is used for the causes of:
questions.exp: The mnemonic lists the causes of fistula-in-ano: Crohn's, trauma (crush), cancer, Koch's (tuberculosis) and immunocompromise. (Book p239)

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a cause of fistula-in-ano?
questions.exp: Crohn's disease, cancer and immunocompromised states are listed. (Book p239)

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical symptom of a perianal fistula?
opts: Staining of the undergarment with pus
questions.exp: Staining of the undergarment with pus and itching are the listed clinical features. (Book p239)

questions.q: On examination of a patient with a perianal fistula the key finding is:
questions.exp: O/E: an external opening is seen on inspection. (Book p239)

questions.q: According to Goodsall's rule, a fistula with its external opening in the anterior half of the anal circumference usually has:
opts: A long curved tract opening in the midline posteriorly
questions.exp: Anterior fistulae run in straight, radial tracts to the internal opening. (Book p239)

questions.q: According to Goodsall's rule, a fistula opening posteriorly has:
opts: A curved tract that opens in the midline
A tract that always crosses the midline anteriorly
questions.exp: Posterior fistulae have curved tracts that open in the midline (posteriorly). (Book p239)

questions.q: The exception to Goodsall's rule is:
opts: A long anterior fistula (>3 cm) which behaves like a posterior fistula
Any fistula secondary to Crohn's disease
questions.exp: A long anterior fistula (>3 cm) is the exception — it curves back and opens in the midline at the 12 o'clock position. (Book p239)

questions.q: A horseshoe fistula is characteristically associated with which type of fistula?
questions.exp: The page mentions a horse shoe fistula occurring with a posterior fistula. (Book p239)

questions.q: The investigation of choice for fistula-in-ano is:
questions.exp: MR fistulogram is the investigation of choice (IOC). (Book p240)

questions.q: Park's classification of fistula-in-ano is based on:
questions.exp: Park's classification is based on the MR fistulogram — i.e. the relation of the tract to the sphincters. (Book p240)

questions.q: The most common type of fistula-in-ano in Park's classification is:
questions.exp: Transsphincteric fistula is the most common (m/c). (Book p240)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Park's four types of fistula?
questions.exp: Park's types are intersphincteric, transsphincteric, suprasphincteric and extrasphincteric; supralevator is an abscess type. (Book p240)

questions.q: The suprasphincteric fistula passes:
opts: Over the top of the external sphincter (above the anorectal ring level of the sphincter complex)
Outside both sphincters without relation to them
questions.exp: Suprasphincteric means the tract passes above the sphincter complex before descending. (Book p240)

questions.q: The extrasphincteric fistula is one that:
opts: Passes outside the sphincter complex from the rectum to the perianal skin
Lies only in the intersphincteric plane
questions.exp: Extrasphincteric fistulae run outside the external sphincter, from the rectum to the perianal skin. (Book p240)

questions.q: The landmark used to classify a fistula as high or low, based on its internal opening, is the:
questions.exp: The landmark is the anorectal ring: above it the fistula is high, below it low. (Book p240)

questions.q: A fistula whose internal opening lies above the anorectal ring is called a:
questions.exp: Above the anorectal ring = high fistula. (Book p240)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four principles of fistula surgery listed?
opts: Routine faecal diversion in every case
Delineate the anatomy of the epithelialised tracts
questions.exp: The principles are: eliminate all septic foci, delineate the anatomy of the epithelialised tracts, preserve continence and prevent recurrence. (Book p240)

questions.q: Fistulectomy involves:
opts: Opening the tract and curetting granulation tissue
questions.exp: Fistulectomy is removal of the entire tract. (Book p240)

questions.q: Fistulotomy is described as:
opts: Opening the tract and removing granulation tissue
Excision of the internal opening alone
questions.exp: Fistulotomy: the tract is opened and granulation tissue removed. (Book p240)

questions.q: An advantage of fistulectomy mentioned in the chapter is that it is:
opts: Free of any risk to continence
questions.exp: Fistulectomy is described as cost effective. (Book p240)

questions.q: Fistulectomy is avoided in a high fistula because:
opts: It damages the sphincter and causes incontinence
It always leaves the internal open
questions.exp: Fistulectomy in a high fistula damages the sphincter and causes incontinence — hence it is avoided. (Book p240)

questions.q: The treatment of choice for a high fistula described here is:
questions.exp: High fistula is managed by seton treatment. (Book p241)

questions.q: A seton is:
opts: A thread inserted into the fistula and tightened at intervals
A rubber band applied above the dentate line
A mesh placed in the ischiorectal fossa
A sclerosant injected into the tract
questions.exp: A thread is inserted into the fistula and tightened over frequent intervals. (Book p241)

questions.q: The advantage of a cutting seton is:
opts: Gradual cutting of the tract with less chance of incontinence
No need for any further surgery
questions.exp: Gradual cutting of the tract gives less chance of incontinence because fibrosis holds the sphincter as it divides. (Book p241)

questions.q: The two types of seton are:
questions.exp: Types: draining seton and cutting seton. (Book p241)

questions.q: A draining seton is preferred in:
questions.exp: A draining seton is used in Crohn's disease (to keep sepsis draining without dividing the sphincter); a cutting seton is used for a high fistula. (Book p241)

questions.q: The material used for a seton is:
questions.exp: Material: prolene suture. (Book p241)

questions.q: In partial (mucosal) rectal prolapse the layer prolapsed is the:
questions.exp: Partial prolapse is a mucosal prolapse; complete prolapse involves all layers. (Book p241)

questions.q: Partial rectal prolapse is typically seen in:
questions.exp: Partial prolapse is seen in children; complete prolapse in adults. (Book p241)

questions.q: Complete rectal prolapse is associated with:
questions.exp: Complete prolapse is associated with a weak pelvic floor; partial prolapse with an incomplete sacral curve. (Book p241)

questions.q: The first episode of a partial prolapse is treated by:
questions.exp: First episode: digital reposition. (Book p241)

questions.q: Recurrent partial prolapse in a child is treated by:
questions.exp: Recurrent cases are treated by Thiersch wiring or sclerotherapy. (Book p241)

questions.q: A 4-year-old child brings out a 3 cm mass after passing stool; the mucosa shows radial folds rather than the concentric rings of a full-thickness prolapse. This is:
questions.exp: Partial thickness prolapse occurs in children and only mucosa prolapses; complete prolapse is full thickness. (Book p241)

questions.q: Compared with perineal procedures, abdominal procedures for complete prolapse are:
opts: More difficult with more operative complications
Associated with a higher recurrence rate
questions.exp: Abdominal procedures are difficult and have more operative complications; perineal ones are easier with fewer complications. (Book p242)

questions.q: Recurrence after an abdominal procedure for prolapse is:
opts: The same as after a perineal repair
questions.exp: Abdominal procedures: recurrence ↓↓; perineal procedures: recurrence ↑↑. (Book p242)

questions.q: Perineal procedures for rectal prolapse are preferred in:
questions.exp: Perineal procedures are used in frail, elderly patients with co-morbidity; abdominal ones in young, fit patients. (Book p242)

questions.q: Which of the following is an abdominal procedure for complete prolapse?
questions.exp: Rectopexy (Well's / Ripstein / Frykman-Goldberg) is the abdominal procedure; Delorme, Thiersch and Altemeier are perineal. (Book p242)

questions.q: Rectopexy means:
opts: Placing a mesh between the rectum and the sacrum
Resection of the redundant sigmoid via the perineum
questions.exp: Rectopexy: mesh placed between the rectum and the sacrum to prevent prolapse. (Book p242)

questions.q: Well's and Ripstein operations are examples of:
questions.exp: Well's and Ripstein are the named rectopexy operations listed. (Book p242)

questions.q: The Frykman-Goldberg operation is a:
questions.exp: Frykman Goldberg is listed as a resection rectopexy. (Book p242)

questions.q: The Altemeier repair is also called:
questions.exp: Altemeier repair = perineal rectosigmoidectomy. (Book p242)

questions.q: In the Altemeier (perineal rectosigmoidectomy) repair the redundant sigmoid is cut in order to:
questions.exp: The redundant sigmoid is cut and this is done to prevent recurrences. (Book p242)

questions.q: Thiersch wiring consists of:
opts: Digital reduction of the prolapse followed by a purse-string suture (wire) around the anus
Placement of a mesh between rectum and sacrum
questions.exp: The prolapse is reduced digitally and the anus is closed with a purse-string suture (wire). (Book p242)

questions.q: Delorme's repair consists of:
opts: Plication of the mucosa and the prolapse
Placement of a mesh in the sacrum
Excision of the full thickness of the prolapse
questions.exp: Delorme's repair: the mucosa and the prolapse are plicated. (Book p242)

questions.q: The most common complication after surgery for rectal prolapse is:
questions.exp: Constipation is listed as the most common (m/c) complication. (Book p243)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a complication of prolapse surgery?
questions.exp: The complications listed are constipation (m/c), haemorrhage, recurrence, fistula (in females), bladder dysfunction and retrograde ejaculation. (Book p243)

questions.q: A rectovaginal fistula after prolapse surgery occurs due to:
questions.exp: Fistula in females is due to erosion into the vagina. (Book p243)

questions.q: Retrograde ejaculation after rectal prolapse surgery is due to injury to the:
questions.exp: Retrograde ejaculation is listed as a complication of pelvic dissection during prolapse surgery (autonomic nerve injury). (Book p243)

questions.q: The ulcer of solitary rectal ulcer syndrome lies on the:
opts: Anal canal below the dentate line
questions.exp: SRUS: ulcer in the anterior wall of the rectum. (Book p243)

questions.q: The ulcer of solitary rectal ulcer syndrome is located how far from the anal verge?
questions.exp: SRUS is located 3-10 cm from the anal verge. (Book p243)

questions.q: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome is described as the starting point of:
questions.exp: The page says it is the starting point of intussusception/prolapse. (Book p243)

questions.q: The characteristic histopathology of solitary rectal ulcer syndrome is:
opts: Fibromuscular obliteration of the lamina propria
questions.exp: Fibromuscular obliteration of the lamina propria is the histological hallmark. (Book p243)

questions.q: Why is a biopsy mandatory in a rectal ulcer?
opts: To look for a fistula track
questions.exp: Ulcer → biopsy → to rule out (r/o) cancer. (Book p243)

questions.q: STARR, used for solitary rectal ulcer syndrome, expands to:
questions.exp: STARR = stapled transanal rectal resection (of the intussusception). (Book p243)

questions.q: An anorectal malformation is defined by:
opts: Absence of a normal anal opening
questions.exp: Anorectal malformation: absence of a normal anal opening. (Book p243)

questions.q: VACTERL association includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: VACTERL = vertebral, anorectal, cardiac, tracheo-oesophageal, renal and limb abnormalities. (Book p243)

questions.q: The letter 'C' in VACTERL stands for:
questions.exp: C = cardiac abnormalities. (Book p243)

questions.q: The best investigation to delineate the anatomy in an anorectal malformation is:
questions.exp: MRI is described as the best investigation to delineate the anatomy. (Book p243)

questions.q: An invertogram is performed after how many hours of birth?
questions.exp: It is done after 24 hours, by which time gas has reached the rectum. (Book p243)

questions.q: In an invertogram the metallic marker is placed:
opts: At the proposed site of the anal opening
questions.exp: A metallic coin is placed at the proposed site of the anal opening. (Book p243)

questions.q: The invertogram X-ray is taken with the baby:
questions.exp: The X-ray is taken in the inverted position. (Book p243)

questions.q: On an invertogram a distance of more than 2 cm between the coin and the gas shadow indicates:
questions.exp: Distance >2 cm = high anorectal malformation; a short distance (<2 cm) = low anomaly. (Book p243)

questions.q: A male infant with an anorectal malformation classically passes faecal matter:
questions.exp: In males: faecal matter passed during urination and recurrent UTI. (Book p244)

questions.q: Recurrent urinary tract infection in a male infant with an anorectal malformation suggests:
questions.exp: Rectourinary (rectovesical / rectourethral) fistulae present with faecal matter in urine and recurrent UTI. (Book p244)

questions.q: In females the anus in a low anomaly is:
questions.exp: In females the anus is abnormally close to the vagina. (Book p244)

questions.q: Which of the following is a HIGH anomaly in males?
questions.exp: High anomalies in males: anorectal agenesis and rectovesical fistula. (Book p244)

questions.q: Rectourethral fistula in a male is classified as:
questions.exp: Intermediate anomaly in males: rectourethral fistula. (Book p244)

questions.q: Rectovestibular fistula in a female is classified as:
questions.exp: Intermediate anomalies in females: rectovestibular fistula and rectovaginal fistula. (Book p244)

questions.q: Rectal atresia in a female is listed under:
questions.exp: High anomalies in females: rectovaginal fistula and rectal atresia. (Book p244)

questions.q: Persistent cloacal anomaly is listed under:
questions.exp: Miscellaneous (in females): anal stenosis and persistent cloacal anomaly. (Book p244)

questions.q: Management of a LOW anorectal malformation is:
opts: Initial diverting colostomy followed by definitive surgery
questions.exp: Low anomaly: definitive surgery. (Book p244)

questions.q: Management of a HIGH anorectal malformation is:
opts: First a diverting colostomy, then definitive surgery
Immediate definitive surgery in the neonatal period
questions.exp: High anomaly: 1st a diverting colostomy and 2nd definitive surgery. (Book p244)

questions.q: PSARP, the definitive surgery for anorectal malformation, expands to:
questions.exp: Definitive surgery: PSARP = posterior sagittal anorectoplasty. (Book p244)

units.title: Surgical Anatomy of the Rectum
units.sec: Surgical Anatomy of the Rectum · p233
units.guide: Start with the rectum itself: a 12-14 cm tube whose upper and lower parts bend to the right and its middle to the left, and whose lower part alone is bare of peritoneum. That last fact is the whole reason a low anterior resection is possible.

units.title: Anal Canal: Landmarks and Epithelium
units.sec: Anal Canal: Landmarks and Epithelium · p233
units.guide: The anal canal is a 4-5 cm gateway with three landmarks - anorectal ring, dentate line and anal verge. Everything the examiner does depends on whether a lesion sits above the dentate line (columnar, adenocarcinoma, painless) or below it (squamous, squamous carcinoma, painful).

units.title: Columns, Crypts and Haemorrhoidal Cushions
units.sec: Columns, Crypts and Haemorrhoidal Cushions · p233
units.guide: Three tiny structures explain three common diseases: the columns of Morgagni (mucosal folds), the cryptoglandular communication that seeds abscesses, and the three vascular cushions of the distal anal submucosa that prolapse to become haemorrhoids at the classical left anterior, right anterior and right posterior positions.

units.title: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters
units.sec: Nerve Supply of the Anal Sphincters · p233
units.guide: Continence is a nerve story. The internal sphincter runs on autonomic fibres (parasympathetic S2-S4, sympathetic L5), while the external sphincter is somatic via the pudendal nerve - and because it is paired, one side can be lost silently but both cannot.

units.title: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE
units.sec: Rectal Examination: Position, Inspection and DRE · p234
units.guide: A good rectal examination is choreography, not force: consent, left lateral position, inspect first, then one finger. Know what the fingertip meets anteriorly in each sex and why a painful fissure stops you before you begin.

units.title: Endoscopic Visualization of the Anorectum
units.sec: Endoscopic Visualization of the Anorectum · p234
units.guide: Instruments only matter if you know how far they reach. Anoscope ~10 cm, proctoscope ~13 cm, a 60 cm instrument that stops at the sigmoid colon, and a 110-140 cm colonoscope that travels from the anal canal to the caecum.

units.title: Haemorrhoids: Pathology and Clinical Features
units.sec: Haemorrhoids: Pathology and Clinical Features · p235
units.guide: Haemorrhoids are dilated vascular channels that bleed arterially and are the commonest cause of bleeding per rectum. The bleed is painless unless the piles are external (below the dentate line) or thrombosed - that single distinction drives the whole history.

units.title: Thrombosed Piles
units.sec: Thrombosed Piles · p235
units.guide: A thrombosed pile is a 5 day self healing lesion that, unlike ordinary haemorrhoids, can actually be felt. Decide between clot evacuation/excision now, or settling it down and returning for definitive surgery a few days to weeks later.

units.title: Grading of Haemorrhoids
units.sec: Grading of Haemorrhoids · p235
units.guide: Grading is pure mechanics: I bleeds, II reduces itself, III needs a finger, IV stays out. Every management decision in the next units hangs off this four-step ladder.

units.title: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids
units.sec: Conservative and Office Management of Haemorrhoids · p236
units.guide: Office treatment is where most piles are cured. Banding strangulates the blood supply, sclerotherapy lifts and fixes the cushion, both are done above the painless dentate line - and both become dangerous if the sclerosant is injected too deep, especially anteriorly in a man.

units.title: Operative Management of Haemorrhoids
units.sec: Operative Management of Haemorrhoids · p236
units.guide: When the pile is grade III or IV the answer is an operation. Match the eponyms to the technique - Milligan-Morgan open, Ferguson closed - and remember that stapled haemorrhoidopexy is named as the surgery of choice, with DGHAL as the Doppler-guided alternative.

units.title: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery
units.sec: Complications of Haemorrhoids and Their Surgery · p237
units.guide: Separate the two complication lists: the operation can bleed, damage the sphincter or recur, whereas the disease itself can thrombose, strangulate, fibrose, ulcerate or - rarely - seed portal pyaemia.

units.title: Anal Fissure: Pathology and Diagnosis
units.sec: Anal Fissure: Pathology and Diagnosis · p237
units.guide: A fissure is a split in the epithelium below the dentate line, classically at 6 o'clock, or at 12 o'clock after obstructed labour. Diagnose it by looking, never by pushing a finger in, and read the chronic triad of skin tag, fissure and hypertrophic papilla.

units.title: Medical Management of Anal Fissure
units.sec: Medical Management of Anal Fissure · p237
units.guide: Healing a fissure means breaking the pain-spasm-ischaemia cycle: fibre, fluids, sitz baths, laxatives, topical anaesthetic, and then a chemical sphincterotomy with diltiazem or nitrate - whose headache is the price of the smooth muscle relaxation.

units.title: Surgical Management of Anal Fissure
units.sec: Surgical Management of Anal Fissure · p238
units.guide: When medicines fail, the surgeon divides the internal sphincter laterally, so it relaxes and the fissure heals; when the sphincter must not be cut, an advancement flap brings healthy skin into the defect.

units.title: Pilonidal Sinus
units.sec: Pilonidal Sinus · p238
units.guide: Pilonidal disease is hairs driven under skin by friction - jeep drivers and barbers rather than surgeons. Treat the acute abscess by drainage and hair removal, then choose a definitive technique that flattens or shifts the natal cleft: Limberg, Bascom or Karydakis.

units.title: Anorectal Abscess
units.sec: Anorectal Abscess · p239
units.guide: Anorectal abscesses are named by the plane they occupy - perianal, intersphincteric, ischiorectal, supralevator. Remember that fluctuation is a late sign here just as it is in parotid, breast and palmar/plantar abscesses, and that inadequate drainage is what creates a fistula.

units.title: Fistula-in-Ano and Goodsall's Rule
units.sec: Fistula-in-Ano and Goodsall's Rule · p239
units.guide: A fistula is the chronic form of that abscess: an internal opening, one or many external openings, and a tract whose behaviour Goodsall's rule predicts from the external opening - with the long anterior fistula over 3 cm the famous exception.

units.title: Investigations and Classification of Fistula-in-Ano
units.sec: Investigations and Classification of Fistula-in-Ano · p240
units.guide: Classify before you cut. Park's four types come from the MR fistulogram, while the simpler high/low split is decided by whether the internal opening sits above or below the anorectal ring, and four principles - clear sepsis, map the tract, keep continence, avoid recurrence - govern the operation.

units.title: Operations for Fistula-in-Ano
units.sec: Operations for Fistula-in-Ano · p240
units.guide: Fistulectomy removes the whole tract and is cheap, but in a high fistula it would take the sphincter with it; fistulotomy merely opens the tract and cures the granulation tissue, trading completeness for safety.

units.title: Seton Treatment of High Fistula
units.sec: Seton Treatment of High Fistula · p241
units.guide: For a high fistula, a seton buys time and safety: a prolene thread tightened at intervals cuts slowly and fibroses behind itself, sparing continence, while a draining seton simply keeps sepsis quiet - the right choice in Crohn's disease.

units.title: Rectal Prolapse: Partial versus Complete
units.sec: Rectal Prolapse: Partial versus Complete · p241
units.guide: Prolapse splits cleanly by age and depth: mucosal prolapse in a child with a flat sacral curve, versus full-thickness prolapse in an adult with a weak pelvic floor. The child's first episode is reduced digitally; recurrence earns wiring or sclerotherapy.

units.title: Surgery for Complete Rectal Prolapse
units.sec: Surgery for Complete Rectal Prolapse · p242
units.guide: For complete prolapse the choice is abdominal or perineal. Abdominal rectopexy (Well's, Ripstein, Frykman-Goldberg) is harder but rarely recurs and suits the fit; the perineal options - Thiersch, Delorme, Altemeier - are gentler for the frail but recur more often.

units.title: Complications of Prolapse Surgery
units.sec: Complications of Prolapse Surgery · p243
units.guide: Every prolapse operation has a price: constipation is the commonest complaint, and pelvic dissection can cost a woman a rectovaginal fistula or a man bladder function and antegrade ejaculation.

units.title: Solitary Rectal Ulcer Syndrome
units.sec: Solitary Rectal Ulcer Syndrome · p243
units.guide: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome is the anterior rectal ulcer 3-10 cm up that marks the start of an internal intussusception - fibromuscular obliteration of the lamina propria on biopsy, always biopsied to exclude cancer, and treated with stapled transanal rectal resection.

units.title: Anorectal Malformation: Assessment
units.sec: Anorectal Malformation: Assessment · p243
units.guide: In the newborn with no anal opening, look for the rest of VACTERL, then image. MRI best defines the anatomy, while the invertogram - done after 24 hours, coin on the proposed anus, baby upside down - turns the coin-to-gas distance into a simple high versus low answer.

units.title: Anorectal Malformation: Classification and Management
units.sec: Anorectal Malformation: Classification and Management · p244
units.guide: Finish by turning the anatomical level into a plan: boys leak stool into urine through rectovesical or rectourethral fistulae, girls present with the anus crowding the vagina, low anomalies go straight to PSARP, and high anomalies are staged behind a diverting colostomy.
